purpose: Define deterministic Topic coverage and classification rules for every active canonical identity, including explicit Outsider handling and the decision process for reusing an existing Topic versus creating a new Topic.

value.name: Decide whether a new Topic is required

value.classification_question: Does this belong under an existing Topic, or should a new Topic be created?

coverage.normal: one or more direct or inherited Topic memberships
coverage.multiple: valid and expected where semantics participate in multiple groupings

outsider.meaning: Canonical identity exists but its Topic classification is intentionally unresolved.

value.purpose: Group classification and coverage validation for canonical identities.

invariants.rule: Every active canonical identity is visible either through direct/inherited Topic membership or explicit Outsider status.
An identity is never forced into a semantically incorrect Topic merely to satisfy coverage.

hard_gates.condition: Active identity has no direct/inherited Topic membership and no explicit Outsider status.
Topic membership is assigned from filename, path, naming similarity or other heuristic rather than explicit semantics.
Existing Topic is reused despite requiring semantic stretching.
Outsider status has no machine-readable reason.
Identity remains Outsider after a valid direct or inherited Topic membership has been established.

references.purpose: Uses canonical Topic membership and inheritance semantics.
Uses deterministic Topic projections for coverage validation.

prose.summary: Makes Topic coverage explicit: reuse an existing Topic when semantically correct, create a new Topic freely when needed, otherwise expose the identity as an Outsider rather than guessing.

Pass 8 formalized previously free Flow actor/data/target/condition/payload/result/error tokens as exact owner-scoped member identities while preserving every source literal.

semantics.identity_rule: This member gives an exact owner-scoped identity to the literal Flow token without adding semantics beyond the owning Flow reference field and the preserved source literal.
semantics.interpretation_rule: Consumers may use this identity as an opaque declared Flow symbol. No meaning may be inferred from spelling, whitespace, filename, path or similarity to another symbol.
semantics.authority_rule: A Flow symbol is descriptive/causal model data only and never grants runtime authority, capability, ownership or execution permission.
semantics.scope_rule: Identity is scoped semantically to the defining contract; identical source literals in another contract or another Flow-ref role are not automatically the same semantic identity.
